title: Faux Optionality (Default Sentinel wrapping Option)
pattern: A function wrapped in an `Option` returns a dummy, "neutral" default value (like `Some(Default::default())`) on invalid inputs, rather than returning `None`.
why_bad: It defeats the purpose of the `Option` type. Callers are forced to write match arms for `None` that will never execute, while simultaneously being exposed to silent errors because invalid inputs yield dummy data blocks instead of forcing empty-set checks.
detection: A return of `Some(t)` where `t` is a sentinel or default-constructed instance, inside a method whose signature is designed to represent nullable or missing results via `Option`.
fix: Return `None` on invalid inputs, forcing callers to explicitly and safely handle the absence of data.
source: Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling made Functional*, Chapter 4 ("Flipping the signature").
